question: Relating components of human milk and immune system, it is FALSE that:

options.opa: Lactoferrin protects against infections due to its ability to bind iron.
options.opb: The casein peptides have antimicrobial and immunostimulant activity.
options.opc: Cytokines modulate the immune system in childhood.
options.opd: Complex oligosaccharides can be false receptors for bacteria in the intestine.
options.ope: Lysozyme degrades the cell walls of gram-negative organisms.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lactoferrin binds iron -> Iron binding inhibits bacterial growth -> Lactoferrin protects against infections -> 95% CHAIN: Casein peptides have antimicrobial activity -> Antimicrobial activity helps fight infections -> 90% CHAIN: Casein peptides have immunostimulant activity -> Immunostimulant activity boosts immune response -> 90% CHAIN: Cytokines modulate immune system in childhood -> Cytokines regulate immune responses -> 95% CHAIN: Complex oligosaccharides mimic receptors for bacteria -> Bacteria bind to oligosaccharides instead of intestinal cells -> False receptors for bacteria in the intestine -> 90% CHAIN: Lysozyme degrades cell walls of gram-negative organisms -> Lysozyme disrupts bacterial cell integrity -> 95%
analysis: Human milk contains various components that play a crucial role in supporting the infant's immune system. It is important to understand the functions of these components to ensure the well-being of the child.
